newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Canada authorizes Argentine beef imports - official.
newsitem.headline: Canada authorizes Argentine beef imports - official.

text.p: Canada and Argentina have signed an agreement authorizing imports of Argentine beef and Canadian pork to their respective countries, an Argentine official said Monday.

"The importance of this is that Canada is recognizing a new sanitary status for Argentina," Carlos Lehmacher, Vice-President of the Argentine government's National Agricultural and Food Health Service, told Reuters.

Argentine beef was for long barred from major markets due to its problems with foot and mouth disease, but the country is now due to be declared foot-and-mouth free within a month by the Paris-based International Epizootic Office.

Lehmacher said that the Argentine government estimates that the country could eventually export as much as 100,000 tonnes a year of beef to Canada, but this would require Argentina to build up its production.
Argentina exported about 470,000 tonnes of beef in 1996.
In another step forward for the image of Aregntine beef, the United States has agreed in principle to allow imports of 20,000 tonnes a year.
The U.S. authorities two weeks ago promised Argentina's Agriculture Secretary Felipe Sola that exports could begin within 60 days, Lehmacher said.
